headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and prompt-injection pathways; RD-Agent’s API use amplifies cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo/user files and can use MCP; RD-Agent can read/write log files and run browser/API workflows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge through shared files or logs, even though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, injected text can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories per agent.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Review and sanitize any file content before one agent hands it to the other.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and user-provided directories; RD-Agent touches logs and can call external APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow into RD-Agent outputs or third-party model calls. The pair’s default broad egress makes leakage materially dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or directory, files readable by Claude Code can be exposed to RD-Agent.
IF RD-Agent sends those contents to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/LiteLLM, leakage leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets and source code out of any shared directory.
Run RD-Agent with redacted inputs only.
Disable outbound API calls for sensitive runs.
Rotate any credentials present in the shared workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can modify git state and write the filesystem; RD-Agent can also write logs and operate concurrently. The profiles do not show locking or coordination between them, so overlapping writes can corrupt shared working state. This is a real default-path conflict, but the blast radius is usually recoverable.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent commits or edits can race.
IF RD-Agent writes logs into a directory Claude Code also edits, file clobbering can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Use separate output directories.
Serialize write access with a simple lock file.
Commit or stash before handing work between agents.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell actions, and git changes; RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can consume outputs and call APIs. If RD-Agent treats Claude Code’s artifacts as authoritative, a bad suggestion can cascade into API-driven research, logs, or downstream actions without verification. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Claude Code output without validation, errors propagate into subsequent research steps.
IF Claude Code writes code or configs that RD-Agent later executes or reports on, the mistake compounds.
mitigations: Require human review before RD-Agent consumes Claude Code output.
Add a checksum or review step for transferred artifacts.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis on handoff files.
Keep action-taking disabled until outputs are verified.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets; RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple external APIs. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so mixed-data workflows can create policy mismatches. Because the compliance surface is broader on RD-Agent, the risk is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as financial reports or secrets are placed into the shared workflow, retention and residency rules must match.
IF either agent logs sensitive inputs longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Purge logs after each run.
Use separate credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
